content: Detaching a long job from its launching client: processes die because the kernel SIGHUPs the terminal session. Three routes. (1) setsid/double-fork (Rust 'daemonize' crate, or nix fork+setsid): gives detachment and log files but NO reattachment channel. (2) tmux detach/reattach: best when you want live observable output and interactive attach; host-affine, not reboot-durable, and a poor supervisor (systemd+tmux needs Type=forking and loses journald capture). (3) systemd-run --user transient unit: strongest supervisor -- restart policy, cgroup limits, systemctl --user status/stop, journald logs; pair with loginctl enable-linger to survive full logout; do NOT double-fork inside the binary under systemd (daemon(7) new-style daemons). Key separation: durability and reattachment are different concerns. Recommended shape is a plain Type=simple foreground binary plus a control channel (unix domain socket + thin 'app attach' subcommand) rather than using tmux as the supervisor. Keep setsid as the portability fallback for macOS/BSD/non-systemd.
